name: London System
blurb: A system rather than a sharp opening: White plays d4, Bf4, e3, c3 and develops calmly against almost anything. Easy to learn and hard to beat, which makes it a club favourite.

ideas.d4: Takes a central square that the queen already supports.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3: Develops the knight and covers e5 before deciding on the rest of the setup.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4: The London bishop comes out before e3, so the pawn will not shut it in behind the chain.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3: Supports d4 and opens the way for the f1 bishop.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2: The knight goes to d2, where it covers e4 and leaves c3 free for the pawn.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 e6 c3: With pawns on c3, d4 and e3, White's centre holds firm against ...c5 and ...Nc6.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 e6 c3 B: Avoids the bishop trade on f4. If Black takes on g3, the h-pawn recaptures and the h-file opens for White's rook.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Bd3: The bishop goes to d3, where it controls e4 and aims at h7.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 e6 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Bd3 Nh: If Black trades the knight for the London bishop, take back with the e-pawn: the f4 pawn covers e5 and the e-file opens for the rook.
ideas.d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3: Against the mirror-image ...Bf5, White keeps the same pawn triangle on c3, d4 and e3.
ideas.d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4: Against a King's Indian setup, White keeps the same plan: bishop out first, then e3, c3 and quiet development.
